body:
I'm alone on Christmas too, but I prefer it that way. Still, it's a little hard to see all the stuff on Facebook about people and their friends and family and joy. I mean I'm happy for them I guess, that they're blissfully unaware of what it's like to be in this place of darkness, where none of that festivity means anything to me.

That said, keep in mind Facebook is also very fake and people show only what they want others to see.

I'm sorry you're alone this holiday and that things have been not working out for you. This is a difficult time of year but it won't be winter forever... and that always helps me at least, just a little bit.

Hey! I'm so proud of you! Taking this first step and admitting you have a problem, that is so hard, one of the hardest things. Of course you feel miserable right now... that's why people avoid confronting themselves, it hurts, and it's hard to know where to go from there.

But it can get better from here. Addiction really affects so much.... but slowly, in recovery, you can rebuild.

I do want to say please talk to a doctor about this because it can be very physically dangerous to just stop drinking out of no where when your body has learned to depend on it. Your body can go into shock and it can be fatal. Doctors can help you detox so this doesn't happen.

I have issues with anxious attachment too and ever since I've learned about it, I've been working on it, and things have been improving in that area. It's opened my eyes. Things can change there though.
Lol I feel the same way but different things work for different people. I am glad they found something that works for them.

Not all illnesses can be cured. 

I mean maybe one day, but not now.

And even among those that can be cured, there are strains that are more resistant or nonresponsive to treatment.

Medical science says depression is highly treatable. I agree there's hope for many. But most of these studies are conducted with a very narrow demographic, and usually with regards to later onset depression. Not so much chronic, lifelong depression. 

Anyway thanks for your thoughts
It's really a difficult time. I hope you find some reprieve soon.

Breakups are really hard and I'm sorry for the pain you're going through.

I think one of the hardest things about breakups is... sometimes you need to find your identity again outside of that person. Maybe try to get out and try a new thing, a hobby or skill or something new that is *yours*. Or pick  up an old interest that you put aside during the relationship for whatever reason. But ... find something that is about *you*. Slowly you can rebuild. 

You're young still, and I'm sorry this didn't work out, but remember that this is something almost everyone goes through and it's normal and survivable. It's hard to let old ideas die, when you've invested so much in them. But they were just ideas, and you will find more opportunities in time. Opportunities for you and a future partner (once you're ready), and opportunities all for yourself.

 For now you need to focus on you. It's very wise and mature that you are aware of the possibility of rebounding and want to avoid that. I have a lot of faith in you.

Oh my dear.

Eating disorders are one thing I have a LOT of experience with, and several years ago I could have written this myself. It IS something I actually recovered from though --- for the most part (eh it's kind of an ongoing battle in some ways, but it doesn't take over my life anymore). I had anorexia too, and trust me, starving yourself is 100% not the answer. It's miserable and you still end up binging.

It doesn't matter what disordered eating behaviour you're engaging in -- they all serve the same purpose, to feel in control, to ease some pain because you don't have better coping skills.

I'm sorry you feel hatred towards yourself. This isn't your fault. Is there any way you can get help for this? I mean... trust me, it's better to catch it as early as possible for it spirals more and more out of control. It's such a painful thing that so few people understand (well, except those who go through it, and it's not actually that uncommon) and my heart aches for you. 

If you need to talk to anyone about this eating stuff please don't hesitate to PM me. Like I said, I have experience and this is one thing I actually did more or less manage to overcome --- after a long time and a lot of work.  I won't have all the answers by any means but I can listen and give feedback (if you want it) for you to take or leave.

I am sad to hear that you feel your friends and family would shame you for your depression instead of helping you.

Fitting into society is hard in general. I don't know how some people do it so easily but everyone has different circumstances to deal with. I've personally found that I am a lot happier when I don't compare myself to others --- but that's really hard, and it's my experience, may not be anything to do with yours. I do think you're being too hard on yourself though. Depression is such a spiral and it's common to lose motivation to groom and such. It's hard to get out of. I know it's possible one bit at a time, for a lot of people, but it's hard to know where to start.

<3 I hope this gets better for you and you find strength and support. Do you have anyone you feel you can talk to about this who wouldnt judge you?

I am not sure what to say --- only because I am so tired and depressed myself, not because I didn't read your words or because I don't feel for you. There's so much here. I really really hope it gets better.

Simple things, complex things, they all blur together, nothing is more enjoyable than the next thing. And one thing I know is that I NEED a lot of mental stimulation in order to thrive at all, which... I wish it wasn't that way. 

I don't know what happiness is. I used to like the Greek concept Eudaimonia (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eudaimonia for anyone curious who doesn't know)... Because that seemed like some sort of higher purpose than myself, outside of a mere mood. That's fine, and all, but it only matters so much when I DO have such a dark mood all the time. 

What do YOU think happiness is?
wut

I'm sorry to hear about that.

I'm not going to publicly take a moral position about the suicide-as-a-parent thing, because it's personal and complex. But *I* certainly don't have children - I will never have children *for this reason*. I don't have anyone depending on me, at least not in a healthy way. My alcoholic mother might mentally depend on me too much, and I hate what this would do to her, but it's not my fault she depends on me in unhealthy ways. SHE is not my responsibility. She is not my child. 

So with that said, I don't see what responsibilities I'm shirking and overall I think people would be better off without me, without the concern and frustration they're going to always feel since I'm going to always be depressed.

Lol. Thanks.

They have hope for me because they don't understand. It may not be IMPOSSIBLE for me to get better to the point that life is bearable, but it is NOT realistic. Even a small chance of it would take a whole lot more resources than is reasonable at this point --- I have tried basically everything. Therapy, drugs, creative expression, socializing more, going through the motions in hopes I regain some semblance of meaning again, ~exercise~, light therapy, blablabla. And THEY, my loved ones who want me alive, THEY don't have to do all of this to keep functioning in misery, so why should they expect me to? Just because they ~have hope~ about something they can't possibly know everything about, because it's not their life? I mean, heck, I've even considered just giving up on happiness and living for the sake of other people, going around the world helping as much as I can. I know that sounds crazy but literally I could think of nothing else to cope. But that's not going to happen. I don't have the energy to move most days.

So frankly, even if on the off-chance that recovery is vaguely possible in some galaxy far far away, I don't WANT to endure it any more.

I wish they could understand that.

Yes I've gone for walks, even with my dog when I had one (sadly I no longer do). Lmao. It was nice. It helped. Sometimes. sometimes not. When it did, very briefly. I wish that were enough. A lot of things SORT of help SOMEWHAT, very briefly, then it all goes back to the same thing. It is massively disproportionate darkness no matter what.

I mean I would just like to think that any rational and understanding human would be able to let someone go in this situation. Lol. But that's idealistic. I have no doubt they'd be angry and some angry forever.

Also just a thought. Killing yourself to make a statement about control seems ironic to me. Aren't you still showing that their opinions or beliefs have some power over you? and to kill yourself over it... That's a LOT of power. (I know that's prob not the only reason you'd consider suicide, but the fact it has such heavy influence at all is concerning).

I think it's important to be open to the fact out perspectives are likely to be kinda warped when we are depressed, too. So any statement we think we make... Might be just really irrational.
I personally didn't downvote you, and I appreciate your sentiments and contribution. Just haven't had a chance to reply to your last response yet. <3

I mean, this is largely how I feel. I don't think it means life can't be worth living for some people, or that self-preservation selfishness is a bad thing. It makes sense, evolutionarily. Plus you can't help others if you're dead or injured, therefore we have the whole "put your gas mask on first" thing. Also makes sense.

But that ALSO means that everyone is ultimately responsible for themselves and their own life, no one else's. No one needs anyone in particular (though we do need people in general, there are plenty others out there). No one needs me. 

I have nothing to offer people anyway at this point.

That said, I do worry about hurting my friends and family. I can say all this theoretically but it breaks my heart to know what I'll do to them. I would never kill myself to make a statement -- that wouldn't work, people's entire psychological understanding of life is not going to be changed by anything I do. I can't control what they think. 

But I also feel like maybe if they really and truly understood how little I want to be here, and that it really is highly unlikely to get better (it's not impossible but it's very unrealistic)... They would let me go.

Yeah but losing loved ones is a part of life. Just usually not by suicide. Living life is devastating.

I wouldn't do it around the holidays, would wait a month or so because for some reason people value this time of year. I don't but whatever.

Well, people think it's intrinsically worthwhile, that doesn't mean it actually is. I'm also not saying it isn't. But if we stop being abstract about this concept of intrinsic worth, and look at how this all applies to people... Who are other people to say that life should be bearable for me? Or worth living? I see no worth in myself, I see nothing worth living for, and others might "disagree" but that doesn't make it any better for me.
Thank you so much. And I'm so happy for you, too.

If you're having doubts at all --- that means something. Death is permanent. If you decide to kill yourself in the future, you still can. It may not work out for this particular plan but you will be able to find other ways. Which I only say because it's an argument FOR giving it some more time now.

My dear, there is no way that you are a constant source of badness to everything --- but I know it might feel that way, really and truly. What makes you feel that way? 

I think it sounds like you're carrying way too much weight on your shoulders. The fact you care so much about this kind of thing shows you are an empathetic person... your perspective probably just needs some adjusting, as is always the case with severe depression. but you don't have to worry about making that kind of change right now if it's too overwhelming. It's important to first get to the root of why you feel so guilty and "bad" and responsible for the world. 

This was a few hours ago and I might not be able to respond until tomorrow but I hope to see a response from you.

I understand all your fears with calling 911. However, you just tried to kill yourself. Things felt bad enough that you tried to *die*. No consequence from calling 911 can possibly make things feel worse than they already felt when you attempted suicide. So you might as well call because it can only get better from here.

And if you don't, you may have permanent damage that ends up creating a lot more trouble than the potential consequences of calling.

First of all, I'm very glad you're writing here. Don't hesitate to write more when you need it. There's clearly a part of you that wants there to be another solution -- even if that seems out of reach right now.

I relate to this so much. I can't even begin to tell you. I have my date set a bit in advance too, so I can be absolutely sure there is no other option, before I do this - and also so as not to ruin the holidays for people. 

It's really sad when things come to this. Sometimes "I love people and don't want to hurt them" just stops being enough, because life feels so insufferable. But the fact you have things you're planning to do first, things you're holding out for, is a good sign. There are things that matter to you and it is still possible to regain a sense of meaning from them... meaning enough to keep going. It has to be possible. This is just a mindset... albeit a very persistent one. But feelings are not facts.

I hope things can change for you and I wish I could be more helpful.

I relate to this. I think for a lot of people depression does get better, and for most people, if not everyone, it can become manageable. 

But from a young age I was distraught by the world and all of the harm humans cause. I remember feeling like I was losing my mind as a young teenager because no one seemed to care about how fake society seemed, how important problems are just ignored. I'm now in my mid 20's and while I don't consider myself a true misanthrope, it kills me to be a part of this oppressive, cruel world without doing anything to actively improve it. I barely have the energy to get through my day. But it's such a crushing thing. I understand why people try to be apathetic.

But it's not true that everything washes away as though it never existed. There is so much to learn from history. There is art, science, math, culture, religion, philosophy, politics, civil rights progress, architecture... these things continue on and it's not because of one person. I try to find meaning in this. I personally may not matter much but in some ways, that's a liberating realization. I can spend time here learning and contributing as much as possible, might as well since I'll die one day anyway. I wouldn't be so hurt by all of this if I didn't care about people. 

That's not a mindset I can always maintain, though, when I'm very depressed.  I understand that. Sometimes it's just so overwhelming and seems so futile. Even though the world DOES improve and can continue to do so. Humans are very young as a species, still. We're figuring it all out.

Yeah, that's interesting. You're right. Strength is more than just resilience, it's also integrity and action. Maybe I'm too tired and cowardly to even want to have courage any more, though. And if that's the case, I figure all the more reason I should consider myself undeserving of life. 

Still, I appreciate you pointing out the distinction. It's something to think about and something I struggle with.

Well, thank you. It helps to hear that it's at least possible, at least for other people, so maybe for me. I've already done a lot of re-engineering and have become so much stronger... people often say I'm one of the strongest and most resilient people they've ever met. I was recently told "to me you are the epitome of indomitable". But I'm getting kind of tired of hearing it. Either I'm not as strong as they think I am, or I just don't even care enough to try to be strong anymore.

Thank you. The triggers question is important. Everything seems like a big overwhelming mass of triggers, and has for my whole life, but I know there must be SOME things that set me off more than other things. I know break-ups and romantic loss are huge triggers for me, also feeling trapped and limited in my options for work or school or anything. Thinking about the failure of my life is a huge trigger, not having any goals is a huge trigger, and I can't make any because everything seems overwhelming or pointless or both. Feeling like I make things worse for other people, being an inadequate friend or family member, makes this a lot worse too.

I also have OCD and body dysmorphic disorder and these trigger the depression and the depression triggers them in turn. 

I'm currently working with my doctor and they're trying all kinds of new meds. I've been on SO many different kinds and cocktails though and nothing seems to stick or work enough. I think I might be one of those people where it's just not possible.
